sentences.text: In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the 'preponderance of probabilities' which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
Further, in holding any inquiry under section 168, The Claims Tribunal may follow such summary procedure as it thinks fit.
10. Now in this case, petitioner Hitesh Singh is the injured and witness of the accident.
In order to establish his claim, he has examined himself as PW-1.

Petitioner deposed on oath that on 07.05.2022, at about 08:00 P.M., he was going to his home on a motorcycle driven by his brother Avinash Singh and offending vehicle bearing No.DL-1-VC-5555 came at a very high speed and hit victim vehicle from back side, resulting in sustaining grievous injuries by the petitioner.
His testimony remained unassailed in cross-examination by counsel for respondents.

Driver/R1 examined himself in defence and deposed that the petitioner had come from Akshardham side at a fast speed and hit his vehicle on left rear wheel of RTV and fell down on the road and that there was no pillion rider on his motorcycle and that petitioner was driving motorcycle in a negligent manner.
The mechanical inspection report of the offending vehicle does not support the testimony of RW1 and there is nothing to suggest any left rear wheel side damage on the RTV.

11. Further, it is not disputed that respondent No.1/driver Rajeev Kumar Jha was charge-sheeted in the aforesaid criminal case for causing the accident by driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner.
Thus, prima-facie, it is clear that respondent No.1 was driving the offending vehicle in a rash and negligent manner at the time of accident.
12. After investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet against respondent no. 1 the driver of the TSR.
Filing of charge-sheet against the driver of offending vehicle prima-facie points to his culpability.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).

sentences.text: If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.

If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.

ISSUE No.2:
16.
Section 168 of the Act enjoins the Claims Tribunal to hold an inquiry into the claim to make an award determining the amount of compensation which appears to it to be just and reasonable.
It has to be borne in mind that the compensation is not expected to be a windfall or a bonanza nor it should be pittance.
17. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.

entities.text: Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It was held in this case that in routine personal injury cases, compensation will be awarded only under the heads-(i) Expenses relating to treatment, hospitalization, medicines, transportation, nourishing food, and miscellaneous expenditure.
(ii) Loss of earnings (and other gains) which the injured would have made had he not been injured ,
comprising (a) Loss of earning during the period of treatment and (iv) Damages for pain, suffering and trauma as a consequence of the injuries.

Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.

What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.

If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though injured may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities consequent to his injuries.

18. Therefore, on the basis of the injuries to the petitioner, the compensation is awarded to the petitioner / injured Hitesh Singh under the aforesaid heads as follows :-
MEDICAL EXPENSES:
19.

Petitioner has not filed all of the original medical bills and as per the verification report filed by the insurance company, an amount of Rs.1,76,052/- has been paid by TPA and amount of Rs.5009/-
has been paid by Delhi Arogya Kosh and an amount of Rs.2,01,071.65/- has been paid by petitioner himself and petitioner had not disputed the verification report.

No copy of any medical insurance policy has been produced before the Court and also considering that all original bills are not produced on record and petitioner does not lay claim to the reimbursed bills, it is considered proper Hitesh Singh vs Rajiv Kumar on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101236889/
5 to grant an amount of Rs.2,01,072/- only (which is not disputed by the insurance company), under this head.

PAIN AND SUFFERING:
20.

Petitioner has deposed in his testimony that after the accident, he was taken to R.K. Hospital and referred from there to Max Hospital, Patparganj Hospital, Delhi, where he was operated twice in the same month.
He remained admitted in Max Hospital from 07.05.2022 to 09.05.2022 and from 11.05.2022 to 17.05.2022.

DAR and charge-sheet consist of only the MLC of the deceased and no other medical document, other than a leave certificate issued by the concerned doctor at Max Hospital, which shows that 20 days medical leaves were provided to the petitioner by Certificate dt.
01.06.2022.
The MLC shows that petitioner was diagnosed with serious injury and provisional diagnosis was 'right foot crush injury'.
Petitioner has filed medical bills/invoice, which show that he was under treatment and consultation in Max Hospital in the same year till November, 2022.
No discharge summary/prescriptions have been filed and proved on record in support of the continued treatment.
It is to note that petitioner suffers from permanent disability due to degloving injury in right foot.
Considering the nature of injuries sustained by petitioner, it can be reasonably assumed that he must have remained under immense pain and suffering for a considerable period of time.
Hence, a sum of Rs.80,000/- is granted to the petitioner towards pain and suffering.

LOSS OF AMENITIES:
21.
Petitioner was aged 26 years old at the time of accident and though he claims to be earning, he failed to establish it on record, as discussed in the succeeding paragraphs.

However, considering that the accidental injuries resulted in permanent disability to the extent of 21% in relation to right lower limb, it can be seen that petitioner has suffered from loss of amenities.

Sustaining of such a permanent disability at such a young age, particularly by a human being, who has been actively involved in sports (even though was not a professional player at the time of accident),
is bound to hamper the quality of life of the petitioner and must have resulted in diminishing of enjoyment of amenities of life., as it can reasonably be assumed that he had inclination for sports and would love to engage in sports activities while maintaining an active lifestyle.
Hence, a sum of Rs. 80,000/- is granted to the petitioner under this head.

LOSS OF INCOME DURING TREATMENT:
22.
Petitioner has claimed to be engaged in the business of sale & purchase of car but not a single document with respect to the business has been produced and proved on record.

In the DAR, IO has mentioned that the petitioner was a businessman but no supporting document is annexed and hence, it is clear that DAR has been prepared only on oral statement of petitioner in this regard.

Petitioner has relied on the ITR for the year 2023- Hitesh Singh vs Rajiv Kumar on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101236889/
6 24, which was submitted after the date of accident in May 2022 and the same was filed / submitted on 14.01.2024 as per the document.

sentences.text: From the ITR itself, it is seen that no loss of business was reported in previous year.
Petitioner himself deposed in his testimony that no ITR was filed prior to this ITR.
Document Mark X is not proved on record by summoning any witness from Income Tax Department.
It is interesting to note that in his cross-examination, the petitioner takes a volte face and testified that he was getting 'salary' from the business being run in the name of his mother.
However, ITR does not reflect any income from salary.

Neither any document was produced to show that mother of the petitioner was running any such business nor is there any document to suggest that petitioner was her employee and getting salary as claimed.
No bank statement of the petitioner has been produced & proved on record.
It is also seen that the sports related activity certificate is last of the year 2014 and hence, it is clear that petitioner was not pursuing any career in sports at the time of the accident.
It is not proved on record that petitioner was either running any business or was employed by his mother in any business being run by her or that her mother was a business woman.

It is interesting to note that in the financial statement filed by the petitioner, he has claimed his parents to be completely dependent on him, without any explanation as to how the mother in whose name the business was running as claimed, could be considered to be the dependent of the petitioner, once claimed to be employed and getting salary from the said business of mother.
Further, not a single document was produced even to ex-facie suggest the existence of any such claimed business of either petitioner or his mother.

Hence, it is clear that petitioner has not come to Tribunal with clean hands and in view of the fact that the contradictory facts stated by him cannot be reconciled, it can only be deduced by the Tribunal that he was not working at the time of accident and the ITR was filed in the succeeding year and relied on in the present case, with a view to support the false claim of the petitioner with respect to his earnings.
Hence, in the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the view that no amount of money is to be given towards loss of income during treatment.

LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY :
23.
The next question that remains to be decided is the compensation with respect to the future loss of income on account of permanent disability of the petitioner.
Under this head, it has to be seen that what could be the future loss of income on account of disability, if there was any functional disability involved.

As per the disability certificate number 1/274(3)/Court Cases/DB/DHAS/2020-21/2607 Ex.PW1/,
petitioner suffers from 21% permanent disability in right lower limb on account of degloving injury.
There is nothing in the testimony of the petitioner to suggest in what manner this disability has affected his day-to- day life and working.
Petitioner has not explained his nature of work.
Further petitioner has brought any evidence to suggest that he was thrown out of job or denied any perks in his job on account of injuries and disability.

Petitioner has not led any evidence to show what work he was doing prior to accident and what work was being done by him in the office post accident, to arrive at any conclusion that petitioner's nature of job had changed drastically to his detriment and that it is due to accident solely.

No one from his department /office was summoned or examined to show even ex facie that nature of job of petitioner was changed by office to his disadvantage due to any incapacity Hitesh Singh vs Rajiv Kumar on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101236889/
7 of the petitioner after the accident.
It is not the plea of the petitioner that he had suffered from any loss of income, increment or promotion on account of accident.

As discussed above, petitioner has miserably failed to prove that he was employed and getting salary from any business being run by his mother, or himself or by anyone else, for the sale and purchase of vehicles.

However, assuming that in case petitioner wishes to engage in any such family business for sale purchase of car or considering his sports related ability and past experience, (even if he is not a professional sportsman), he may employ his skills and past experience in any sport related endeavour in some other capacity than sportsman and further considering that neither the petitioner is in any permanent job as claimed by him, nor is there any submission made to suggest that he is preparing for any permanent job, the permanent disability sustained by him shall certainly cause hindrance and adversely impact career prospects of the petitioner either as a businessman or employee in any business, relating to sale purchase of car, as it shall involve outdoor activity to some extent and further petitioner shall be hindered in pursuit of an active lifestyle to some extent.
Hence, the functional disability of the petitioner is being taken as 12% in relation to whole body of the petitioner for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of income of petitioner.

The Tribunal is of the considered view that a balanced approach should be taken and as petitioner proved his educational qualification Ex.PW1/C, according to which he was 12th pass, his salary is estimated as per the minimum wages applicable to an skilled worker in Delhi at the time of accident, as petitioner is stated to be a resident of Delhi and stated to be working at Delhi, which is Rs.20,019/- per month.
On the basis of his future income taken as Rs.20,019/- per month, the petitioner's annual income shall be taken as Rs.2,40,228/- for calculation of loss of future income.

24. The copy of Aadhar card of the petitioner shows that date of birth of petitioner is 10.08.1995,
which would mean that he was around 26 years of age at the time of accident and thus, multiplier of 17 would be applicable.

Further, an addition of income of injured for future prospects to the extent of 40% has to be considered as the age of the petitioner was under the age of 40 years (National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Pappu Dev Yadav vs Naresh Kumar and others 2010 SCC online SC 752 and Sohan Lal vs. Taj Khan & Ors., 2019 ACJ 252, Rajasthan High Court).

sentences.text: The yearly income of the petitioner has been assessed as Rs.2,40,228/-.
In this after adding 40% of the future prospects amounting to Rs.96,091.2/-, the yearly income with future prospects will become Rs.3,36,319/-.
In this, yearly income, a multiplier of 17 will make the future income as Rs.3,36,319 x 17= Rs.57,17,426/-.
Loss of income on account of 12% percent functional disability will mean that the overall loss of income to the petitioner shall be 12% of Rs57,17,426/-, which comes to Rs.6,86,091/-.
Therefore, a sum of Rs.6,86,091/- is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

attendant and special diet charges.

Hence, an inference can be drawn that petitioner had to spend considerable amount to visit hospital / doctor number of times during his treatment.
Thus, the petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.15,000/- towards conveyance.

27. Further, it cannot be ignored that family members of the petitioner must had to render their services for providing assistance to the petitioner in his routine activities and that was bound to suffer their work / job.

For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant / care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.

28. Thus, a total sum of Rs.55,000/- (15,000+20,000+20,000) is awarded to the petitioner under this head.

29. There is no photograph placed on record and no evidence led to suggest how the petitioner on account of the injuries sustained and disability in question, is also suffering from disfigurement of his body and hence, no amount is granted in this aspect.

hence an amount of Rs.30,000/-
is granted to the petitioner under this head.

(INTEREST):
33.
Petitioner has pursued his case since the year 2022.
Therefore, he is entitled for interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization.
34. Now, the question arises as to which of the respondents is liable to pay the compensation amount.
As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured, the Insurance company is liable to compensate the third party.

The insurance company has examined a witness to prove the objections raised by it and to prove that term or condition of insurance policy was breached/ violated by insured as the driver of the offending vehicle was not having commercial valid and effective driving licence at the time of accident.
Driving licence R-1/ Rajiv Kumar Jha is on record and the same shows that he had a valid driving licence for non transport on the date of the accident.
He was not challaned for offence under section 3/181 M.V. Act, as per the charge-sheet.
It is observed that only defence taken by insurer is that the respondent No. 1 was not having commercial DL with appropriate endorsement for driving RTV.
The copy of the registration certificate of the offending vehicle shows that the gross weight / unladen weight of the vehicle was 2840 kgs and hence it was a light motor vehicle.

The issue has been settled by the Supreme Court in the decision given in the case titled as "Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., 2017 ACJ 2011" by holding that the driver holding DL to drive LMV can drive transport vehicles of that class without any endorsement to that effect.

entities.text: Mukund Dewangan Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., 2017 ACJ 2011
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: In view of this, the plea of insurance company that driving of the offending vehicle by R1 without endorsement on his DL regarding commercial vehicle would amount to breach of insurance policy, is not sustainable.
In view of above, it is held that respondent no.3/ insurer shall be entitled to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners.

RELIEF:
35.

In view of the findings on above points, I as presiding officer of this Tribunal award a total compensation of Rs.11,32,163/- (Rupees Eleven Lakhs Thirty Two Thousand One Hundred Sixty Three only) along with interest @ 7.5% per annum on the aforesaid award amount from the date of filing of the petition till realization in favour of petitioner against the respondent no.3/ insurer.
This award is required to be deposited with this Tribunal within 30 days.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
In an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and in fact is the 'preponderance of probabilities' which is applied in civil cases.
It is also the law that the tribunal is not bound by the technical rules of evidence.
12. After investigation, the police filed the charge-sheet against respondent no. 1 the driver of the TSR.
(New India Assurance Company Ltd vs Smt. Washeema Bano (2022) SCC OnLine All 403 and Mangla Ram vs Oriental Insurance Company Ltd (2018) 5SCC 656).
If any party does not accept such charge-sheet, the burden must be on such party to adduce evidence.
If the Tribunal feels that charge-sheet is collusive, it can record that charge-sheet cannot be accepted and call upon the parties at any stage to adduce oral evidence of accident and alleged negligence.
In such cases, issue of negligence must be decided on other evidence ignoring the charge-sheet.
17. The case of Raj Kumar vs Ajay Kumar & Another (2011) 1 SCC 343, is one of the most prominent judgments of the Hon'ble Supreme Court which deals with compensation in injuries cases.
Where the claimant suffers a permanent disability as a result of injuries, the assessment of compensation is also to be done under the head of loss of future earnings which would depend upon the effect and impact of such permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured.
The tribunal should not mechanically apply the percentage of permanent disability as the percentage of economic loss or loss of earning capacity.
What requires to be assessed by the tribunal is the effect of the permanent disability on the earning capacity of the injured after assessing the loss of earning capacity in terms of percentage of the income.
It has to be quantified in terms of money to arrive at the future loss of earnings by applying standard multiplier method.
All injuries or permanent disabilities arising from injuries do not result in loss of earning capacity.
If there is no loss of employment or earning capacity, there may not be any need to award any compensation under the head of loss of future earnings, though injured may be awarded compensation under the head of loss of amenities consequent to his injuries.
Sustaining of such a permanent disability at such a young age, particularly by a human being, who has been actively involved in sports (even though was not a professional player at the time of accident),
is bound to hamper the quality of life of the petitioner and must have resulted in diminishing of enjoyment of amenities of life., as it can reasonably be assumed that he had inclination for sports and would love to engage in sports activities while maintaining an active lifestyle.
It is not proved on record that petitioner was either running any business or was employed by his mother in any business being run by her or that her mother was a business woman.
Further, not a single document was produced even to ex-facie suggest the existence of any such claimed business of either petitioner or his mother.
Hence, it is clear that petitioner has not come to Tribunal with clean hands and in view of the fact that the contradictory facts stated by him cannot be reconciled, it can only be deduced by the Tribunal that he was not working at the time of accident and the ITR was filed in the succeeding year and relied on in the present case, with a view to support the false claim of the petitioner with respect to his earnings.
Hence, in the totality of facts and circumstances of the case, this Tribunal is of the view that no amount of money is to be given towards loss of income during treatment.
LOSS OF FUTURE INCOME ON ACCOUNT OF PERMANENT DISABILITY :
23.
Under this head, it has to be seen that what could be the future loss of income on account of disability, if there was any functional disability involved.
Petitioner has not led any evidence to show what work he was doing prior to accident and what work was being done by him in the office post accident, to arrive at any conclusion that petitioner's nature of job had changed drastically to his detriment and that it is due to accident solely.
No one from his department /office was summoned or examined to show even ex facie that nature of job of petitioner was changed by office to his disadvantage due to any incapacity Hitesh Singh vs Rajiv Kumar on 9 June, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/101236889/
7 of the petitioner after the accident.
It is not the plea of the petitioner that he had suffered from any loss of income, increment or promotion on account of accident.
However, assuming that in case petitioner wishes to engage in any such family business for sale purchase of car or considering his sports related ability and past experience, (even if he is not a professional sportsman), he may employ his skills and past experience in any sport related endeavour in some other capacity than sportsman and further considering that neither the petitioner is in any permanent job as claimed by him, nor is there any submission made to suggest that he is preparing for any permanent job, the permanent disability sustained by him shall certainly cause hindrance and adversely impact career prospects of the petitioner either as a businessman or employee in any business, relating to sale purchase of car, as it shall involve outdoor activity to some extent and further petitioner shall be hindered in pursuit of an active lifestyle to some extent.
Hence, the functional disability of the petitioner is being taken as 12% in relation to whole body of the petitioner for the purpose of assessing corresponding loss of income of petitioner.
Further, an addition of income of injured for future prospects to the extent of 40% has to be considered as the age of the petitioner was under the age of 40 years (National Insurance Company Limited vs Pranay Sethi and others (2017) 16 SCC 680, Pappu Dev Yadav vs Naresh Kumar and others 2010 SCC online SC 752 and Sohan Lal vs. Taj Khan & Ors., 2019 ACJ 252, Rajasthan High Court).
However, it is to kept in mind that petitioner suffered such injures as resulted in prolonged treatment, including hospitalization.
Thus, it cannot be disputed that the petitioner must have spent reasonable amount for his special diet for the purpose of early recovery post surgery.
For claiming compensation, necessity of employing a professional attendant / care taker is not required and the petitioner should be compensated for the value of services of the family members, which has been or would be necessitated by the wrong doing of the driver.
(Refer :
DTC & Ors Vs. Lalita, 1983 ACJ 253).
As insurance company has contractual and statutory liability to indemnify the insured, the Insurance company is liable to compensate the third party.

The yearly income of the petitioner has been assessed as Rs.2,40,228/-.
In this after adding 40% of the future prospects amounting to Rs.96,091.2/-, the yearly income with future prospects will become Rs.3,36,319/-.
Thus, petitioner is granted a sum of Rs.20,000/- towards special diet.
